research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical publications and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Cohort period
verified_claims: The bulletin covers offenders entering the proven-reoffending cohort from April to June 2024.
limitations: The figures describe a historic cohort, not current local risk.

sources.name: Cohort inclusion
verified_claims: The cohort includes releases from custody, non-custodial convictions and cautions.
limitations: The cohort excludes people without a qualifying disposal.

sources.name: Follow-up period
verified_claims: Proven reoffending is measured over one year.
limitations: Offending outside the follow-up window is not included in the rate.

sources.name: Waiting period
verified_claims: A further six-month waiting period allows reoffences to be proven in court.
limitations: The publication necessarily lags the cohort date.

sources.name: Policy context
verified_claims: The cohort is affected by court recovery, Probation Reset, ECSL and recall-policy changes.
limitations: The effect of each policy cannot be isolated from the overall rate.

sources.name: Overall proven-reoffending rate
verified_claims: The April to June 2024 cohort had a proven reoffending rate of 29.6%.
limitations: The rate is not a prediction for an individual offender or property.

sources.name: Quarterly rate change
verified_claims: The overall rate was 0.7 percentage points higher than the previous quarter.
limitations: Quarter-to-quarter movement can reflect cohort mix and operational changes.

sources.name: Annual rate change
verified_claims: The overall rate was 2.1 percentage points higher than the same quarter a year earlier.
limitations: The change cannot be attributed to a single policy or offence trend.

sources.name: Adult rate
verified_claims: Adult offenders had a proven reoffending rate of 29.5%.
limitations: Adult and child cohorts differ in size, disposals and offence mix.

sources.name: Child rate
verified_claims: Child offenders had a proven reoffending rate of 32.8%.
limitations: The child rate must not be converted into a prediction about a particular child.

sources.name: Reoffence frequency
verified_claims: Reoffenders committed an average of 5.13 proven reoffences.
limitations: The average is conditional on reoffending and is not the cohort-wide average.

sources.name: Cohort size
verified_claims: The cohort contained approximately 86,000 offenders.
limitations: Rounded cohort size is not an exact record count.

sources.name: Reoffender count
verified_claims: Around 25,000 cohort members were proven reoffenders.
limitations: This count follows the publication's proof and waiting-period rules.

sources.name: Reoffence total
verified_claims: The reoffenders committed almost 131,000 proven reoffences.
limitations: Multiple reoffences can be attributed to one person.

sources.name: Custody-or-court-order rate
verified_claims: Adults released from custody or starting court orders had a 37.5% reoffending rate.
limitations: The group combines different disposals and offender characteristics.

sources.name: Under-12-month custody rate
verified_claims: Adults released from sentences under 12 months had a 67.1% proven reoffending rate.
limitations: Sentence-length groups are not randomly assigned and cannot establish causal sentence effectiveness.

sources.name: Twelve-month-plus custody rate
verified_claims: Adults released from sentences of 12 months or more had a 23.2% proven reoffending rate.
limitations: Differences from shorter sentences reflect case and offender selection as well as sentence length.

sources.name: Youth-caution rate
verified_claims: Children given youth cautions had a 22.7% proven reoffending rate.
limitations: Disposal groups should not be ranked without controlling for offender characteristics.

sources.name: Youth-custody rate
verified_claims: Children released from custody had a 66.0% proven reoffending rate.
limitations: Custody cohorts are selected for more serious or complex cases.

sources.name: Sentence-comparison warning
verified_claims: The bulletin explicitly warns against comparing sentence effectiveness without controlling for offender characteristics.
limitations: Published disposal rates must not be interpreted as causal effects.
